items.title: Define canonical scope boundary model for story execution
items.context: Create or extend core runtime structures so allowed scope, excluded scope, execution boundary, stop conditions, and allowed file patterns are represented as first-class data consumed by scope checks rather than prose-only plan text.
items.userSees: Running lattice scope_contract_check --json on an undeclared source edit now includes a stable scope row with id, status, source path, blocking=true, and a concrete next-action hint.

happy.desc: Canonical scope contract data represents allowed modifies, allowed creates, allowed tests, protected files, explicit excludes, related docs, and execution-boundary categories as first-class fields consumed by scope checks.
A declared source/docs change is classified through the canonical boundary model and produces stable scope check rows with id, status, source path, blocking flag, and next-action hint.

edge.desc: Unknown or malformed path classes fail closed with a structured reason instead of being implicitly allowed.
Runtime, lifecycle, generated artifact, external authority, direct story JSON, and fixture exclusions remain represented as data and are not collapsed into prose-only plan text.

adversarial.desc: An undeclared runtime source edit and an arbitrary metadata JSON file under a runtime-like directory both block unless the canonical model explicitly permits them.
Scope checks, guard sessions, and operator-facing scope messages consume the same classifier/table rather than maintaining duplicate ad hoc rule sets.

items.title: Harden lifecycle artifact and path classification in scope checks
items.context: Wire lifecycle artifact/path classification into existing scope guard/check behavior so generated story evidence, runtime artifacts, docs, and source changes are interpreted by the same classifier instead of ad hoc path rules.
items.userSees: Running lattice scope_contract_check on lifecycle metadata skips only registered story artifacts, while a nearby unregistered metadata file appears as a blocking scope row instead of being silently exempted.

happy.desc: Registered current-story lifecycle artifacts and registered runtime artifacts are classified as provenance/runtime paths and do not create product scope violations.
Scope contract checks, guard session checks, phase gates, and scope-contract handler output expose stable row fields for classifier decisions: id, status, detail/source, hint, and blocking flag.

edge.desc: Legacy story-tree paths are treated only through the supported legacy metadata path rules, while obsolete story-dir prefixes such as .koala/story are not accepted as lifecycle artifacts.

Nearby but unregistered files such as story evidence notes, arbitrary nested evidence files, unknown metadata JSON, and arbitrary .koala JSON fall through to normal scope enforcement and block when undeclared.

adversarial.desc: The classifier does not introduce blanket exemptions for .lattice, .koala, docs, docs/story, or evidence directories; arbitrary sibling files remain blocking.
Lifecycle artifact classification cannot satisfy delivery, summary, review, validation, or DONE gate receipts; those gates still require their own signed or structured evidence.

items.title: Add structured scope drift repair and fallback behavior
items.context: When a scope check detects drift, expose deterministic repair/fallback guidance and structured evidence without letting the current agent silently expand scope or self-authorize unrelated work.
items.userSees: Running lattice scope_contract_acknowledge prints the affected paths, reason, current head/material hashes when available, and keeps the scope check at warn so reviewers can see the exceptional expansion.

happy.desc: A valid DEV or REVIEW scope acknowledgement for a necessary late expansion records affected paths/items, explicit reason, actor/session, phase, head hash, material hash when available, and structured audit evidence.

After a valid acknowledgement, the same acknowledged paths are surfaced as review-visible scope expansion rather than a silent normal pass, and lifecycle progress still depends on reviewer acceptance.

edge.desc: Acknowledgement or repair requests missing a reason, using malformed paths or evidence refs, targeting terminal phases, or violating phase policy are rejected with deterministic repair/fallback guidance.
A broad or plan-invalidating scope change remains blocking and points back to PLAN or reviewer decision instead of being accepted as a local acknowledgement.

adversarial.desc: The main implementation agent cannot self-sign reviewer-only scope evidence, silently expand the frozen contract, or overwrite authored scope/intent without explicit replace semantics.
Fallback behavior for missing reviewer or unsupported host is visibly lower assurance and never receives the same label or gate meaning as independent reviewer evidence.

items.title: Verify wave 1 with focused regression coverage and synchronized docs
items.context: Add narrow tests and documentation updates proving the M1-M3 behavior works and that later roadmap milestones remain non-goals for this story.
items.userSees: Running npm --prefix packages/main run build and the focused scope smokes passes, and the docs name the new row/classifier/acknowledgement behavior without claiming later roadmap milestones are done.
